```{.quiz-yaml}
id: 11_t_test_grouped_frequencies
title: >
  Why group the scores?
questions:
  - id: grouped_histogram_reason
    type: free-response
    prompt: >
      Why might we use a grouped frequency table and histogram for the class
      reaction-time scores? What might happen if we used much narrower or
      much wider intervals than 20 milliseconds?
    answer: >
      Reaction-time scores can have many distinct values. Grouping them into
      intervals makes the overall shape easier to see, although it sacrifices exact
      score information. Narrower intervals show more detail but can make
      the histogram look fragmented; wider intervals give a simpler picture
      but can hide features of the distribution.
    explanation: >
      Grouped displays are useful when raw or ungrouped frequencies are too detailed
      to reveal the pattern clearly. Twenty milliseconds is a choice that
      balances detail and readability, not a uniquely correct interval width.
      A histogram shows frequencies across adjacent numerical intervals;
      a bar chart is used to compare separate categories.
```
